findings.finding: UK DIY/trade peers reported firm summer-autumn trading: Wickes Q3 (to 26 Sep) Retail LFL +5.6% with DIY in mid-single-digit growth and TradePro +8%, Toolstation UK Q3 LFL +3.6% (Jul-Sep), Howdens UK pro-forma +1.8% (14 Jun-31 Oct) with record TradeFest; positive read-across to B&Q and Screwfix (UK&I ~55% of group) for Q3 Aug-Oct.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 25/26 UK LFL +3.0% with an upgrade: +5.98% on the day; H1 26/27 Screwfix +5.6% with an upgrade: +12.43%
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: these were public RNS on 15 Oct, 20 Oct and 5 Nov and KGF rose from 331p (14 Oct) to 389p since. What keeps a residue: Wickes' quarter ends 26 Sep while Kingfisher's runs to 31 Oct, and B&Q laps a +2.8% Homebase-boosted comparator, so the read-across is partial; if fully priced the stock would not have needed to keep climbing after the Howdens update, which it did (+4.0% on 4 Nov).
findings.independence: Travis Perkins Q3 Toolstation UK LFL +3.6% https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/travis-perkins--tpk/travis-perkins-third-quarter-trading-update/9823575 ; Howdens https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/howden-joinery-group--hwdn/trading-update/9859104

findings.finding: The broad UK series is flat: BRC-KPMG non-food sales 0.0% y/y in October 2026 (4 Oct-31 Oct), 3-month average -0.1%, in-store non-food -1.1%, with big-ticket furniture weak; and Grafton's GB merchanting average daily LFL was -5.2% for Jul-Oct.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 24/25 (softer UK backdrop plus a budget cost warning): -13.2% on the day
findings.why_not_priced: Public macro data; sized small and further cut because it argues against a 9.9% disclosed short only weakly and B&Q/Screwfix have outperformed this series for several quarters. If the market were pricing a UK miss, the stock would not be at a 52-week high into the print.

findings.finding: Iberia remains strong: Grafton's Iberia average daily LFL +7.4% (pro forma +9.0%) for Jul-Oct 2026, consistent with Brico Depot Iberia's Q2 +8.6%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Iberia is ~3% of group sales and has not been the swing line in any recorded reaction
findings.why_not_priced: Probably priced and too small to matter; filed because it is a sourced counterparty datum. Net of the rest of the company it is worth a tenth of a point at most.

findings.finding: French household goods consumption fell 0.5% in volume in both August and September 2026, manufactured goods -1.1% in September (Q3 manufactured goods only +0.3% q/q), a soft backdrop for Castorama and Brico Depot (~30% of sales), partly offset by an easy France comparator (-2.5% LFL in Q3 25/26).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: France has been weak for two years (H1 26/27 France -2.5% in Q2) and the stock still rose 12.4% on H1; France weakness is the known drag
findings.original_quote: La consommation de biens fabriqués se replie (-1,1 % après +0,8 %) ... Sur l'ensemble du troisième trimestre 2026, la consommation des ménages en biens augmente de nouveau (+0,4 % après +0,2 % au deuxième trimestre) — 'Manufactured goods consumption fell (-1.1% after +0.8%) ... over Q3 2026 household goods consumption rose again (+0.4% after +0.2% in Q2)'
findings.why_not_priced: Macro-to-company transmission only; France weakness is the consensus view of this stock, so a weak France is the expected case and is sized small. Samse's Le Bricolage (+11.8% reported Q3, but 9-month group LFL +0.4%) points the other way on the DIY channel.

findings.finding: Guidance arithmetic: FY25/26 adj PBT GBP560m less H1 25/26 GBP368m puts H2 25/26 at ~GBP192m; the new GBP595-635m guide less H1 26/27 GBP404m implies H2 GBP191-231m, so the GBP615m midpoint already needs H2 PBT ~+10% against an H1 that grew +6.1% excluding the GBP14m one-off, which leaves limited room for a second consecutive upgrade.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 guidance changes: Nov 2025 upgrade +5.98%; Nov 2024 profit warning -13.2%; H1 Sep 2026 upgrade +12.43%
findings.why_not_priced: An inference from primary documents, not a disclosed number: the market's expectation of an upgrade is unsourced, but a +22% run since 9 Oct on a name that upgraded at the last two events suggests one is partly expected. The guide's key assumptions also list 'GBP13m non-recurring 2025/26 losses', which if they fell in H2 25/26 lower the base and make +10% easier, so this is sized small and further cut because it argues against a crowded short.

findings.finding: The 28 Oct 2026 Budget announced a two-year real-terms freeze in business rates for all retail, hospitality and leisure properties from April 2027, a cost tailwind for B&Q's and Screwfix's estate that the Q3 statement may reference when commenting on FY27/28.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Budget-driven cost items have moved this name before: Nov 2024 Q3 warned of a GBP45m budget hit and fell 13.2%
findings.why_not_priced: Public for four weeks and KGF fell 2.65% on Budget day, so the market did not reward it then; its value depends on the company quantifying it, which a Q3 statement often does not. Small.

baseline_tension: Mostly agrees with the lean (+2.79, driven by the crowded short) and the run-up (+8.7% 20d, +22.8% 60d): peer evidence is positive but already reflected in the climb, and the guidance arithmetic and soft France cut mildly against it, so the findings net to about zero.
language_note: nothing the English sources did not already carry: the UK's domestic half here was RNS via Investegate (Kingfisher, Wickes, Travis Perkins, Howdens, Grafton) and the FCA register, all of which the international wires also carry for a FTSE 100 name with 18 analysts; the one non-English item (INSEE's French goods-consumption release) is a public macro series, not a domestic-UK source
lessons_applied: 'The move is in the guide' plus 'understatement is the hunters' systematic error': Kingfisher changed its guide at both prior Q3 updates and at H1, and the Q3 numbers are not pre-released, so abs_move_pct went from 5.5 to 7.0 (the 7% new-numbers base; not 9 because a change is possible rather than likely and the name is well covered)
'A narrow proxy loses to a broad series': the peer read-across (Wickes/Toolstation) is cut from +0.6 to +0.4 because the broad BRC non-food series was flat

'Positioning is the thing to beat' / core table (crowded short against a negative): the two negatives that rest on proxy or inference (UK macro -0.3 to -0.2, guidance arithmetic -0.3 to -0.2) and France (-0.2 to -0.15) were made smaller
